route: 1 (published per-item statistics: Table 2 factor loadings, refit) + 3 (published subscale alphas) + nonparametric bootstrap of the assignment
evidence: Re-ran the paper's own analysis: PCA + varimax, 8 factors, on all 44 final-form columns of the S3 File .sav (n=582 complete cases, the paper's own n), then compared each readingK column's full 8-loading profile with the Table 2 rows published for questionnaire items 10-15. Components were labelled by their dominant NON-reading source block wherever possible, and reading6's own assignment was never used to define any component. Observed vs published on the reading factor: reading1 .700/.717, reading2 .733/.732, reading3 .707/.710, reading4 .698/.696, reading5 .570/.534, reading6 .307/.301; on the understanding factor reading6 is .499 vs the published .488 for item 15, and reading5 carries the item-14 access cross-loading .437 vs published .439. Euclidean distances on the diagonal: reading1->item10 0.147, reading2->item11 0.049, reading3->item12 0.035, reading4->item13 0.026, reading5->item14 0.098, reading6->item15 0.102. Column-wise argmin IS the diagonal for all six (every published item's nearest observed column is the claimed one), and over all 720 permutations the identity is the global minimum-cost assignment, SSE 0.04596 vs 0.07180 for the runner-up (a reading3/reading4 swap), a 1.6x margin. Point-estimate row-wise argmin fails at exactly one cell: reading1 sits 0.147 from item10 but 0.139 from item12, an 0.008 difference. A 200-replicate nonparametric bootstrap (resampling the 582 cases, refitting PCA+varimax(8), relabelling components, recomputing the minimum-cost assignment) resolves that cell and every other one: the claimed pairing is the modal answer for all six columns and beats its runner-up in every case -- reading1->item10 80.5% (next 8.5%), reading2->item11 89.8% (5.9%), reading3->item12 87.3% (6.8%), reading4->item13 86.4% (5.9%), reading5->item14 95.8% (2.5%), reading6->item15 99.2% (0.8%). Block membership is separately and order-invariantly confirmed by Cronbach alpha against Table 3: reading1-5 = 0.857 vs published reading .86, and understand1-9 + reading6 = 0.892 vs published understanding .89 (rivals: reading1-6 = 0.855, understand1-9 = 0.887, neither matching a published subscale size). Every item is therefore distinguished from every other. What this does NOT establish: the option_text<->resp axis, which is fixed by the .sav's own value labels (1=never ... 5=always) and the questionnaire's ascending column order rather than by any statistic here; and it does not show that the 47-item pilot administration worded these six items character-for-character as the deposited 44-item final form does -- only that the same six items, in this order, are the pilot 'reading' columns.

route: 1 (published per-item statistics: Table 2 factor loadings, reproduced) + 8 (content-implied correlational predictions)
evidence: Re-ran the paper's own analysis -- PCA + varimax, 8 factors, on the 44 retained columns of the S3 .sav (582 complete cases, the paper's n) -- and compared each of the ten understanding-factor columns (reading6, understand1..9) to Table 2's published rows for items 15-24 over the seven identifiable factors. The minimum-cost (Hungarian) assignment of columns to published rows is EXACTLY the claimed identity map, with per-pair distances reading6->15 0.035, understand1->16 0.139, understand2->17 0.108, understand3->18 0.078, understand4->19 0.036, understand5->20 0.099, understand6->21 0.037, understand7->22 0.101, understand8->23 0.105, understand9->24 0.105 (total 0.8447). Forbidding each claimed pair in turn and re-optimising costs an excess of 0.297 (reading6/15), 0.160 (u3/18), 0.157 (u4/19), 0.256 (u5/20), 0.205 (u6/21), 0.414 (u7/22), 0.153 (u9/24) -- but only 0.026 for u1/16, 0.026 for u2/17 and 0.030 for u8/23. Two content-implied predictions that use no loadings resolve u8 and corroborate u5: (a) item 23 is the third media item, and understand8's mean correlation with the two known media items understand6/understand7 is 0.58 against 0.40-0.46 for every other item in the block; (b) item 20 is about nutrition panels, and understand5's mean correlation with the instrument's two other nutrition-panel items (use1 = item 30, num1 = item 42) is 0.22 against 0.09-0.16 for the rest. NOT ESTABLISHED, which is why this is PARTIAL and not VERIFIED: understand1 and understand2 (items 16 'most things I hear about health' and 17 'the content of health information that I find') are not distinguished from one another. Their loading distances are near-tied (u1: 0.139 to item16 vs 0.140 to item17; u2: 0.108 to item17 vs 0.130 to item16), the excess cost of denying either is 0.026, and a 300-replicate nonparametric bootstrap of the same EFA (176 replicates in which the eight rotated components labelled uniquely) makes item16's modal partner u2 (31.8%) rather than u1 (22.2%), with u1 itself modal on item23 (28.4%) -- i.e. the route does not settle the 16/17 order and only weakly settles u1 against u8. The bootstrap does back the rest: u7->22 99.4%, u5->20 88.1%, reading6->15 84.1%, u3->18 73.9%, u6->21 69.3%, u4->19 66.5%, u9->24 56.8%, u8->23 47.2% (modal in every case). Ordering of u1/u2 therefore rests on the non-data argument that the final questionnaire preserved the pilot form's within-block order, which holds for every other block of the instrument. Also not established: the option_text<->resp axis, which is fixed by the .sav's own value labels (1=never...5=always) and needs no inference, and that the pilot administration worded these nine items character-identically to the deposited final form.

route: route 1 (published per-item statistics -- the 8-factor varimax loading matrix of Table 2), re-run on the raw S3 .sav
evidence: Re-ran the paper's PCA (8 factors, varimax) on all 47 raw item columns. Ten items of undisputed identity (reading 10-14, appraisal 25-29) reproduce Table 2 to max|diff| = 0.044 over factors 1-7, which calibrates the run. Each use column then matches exactly one published row and by a wide margin: use1 -> item 30 (max|diff| 0.045 vs 0.181 for the runner-up), use2 -> item 31 (0.054 vs 0.173), use3 -> item 32 (0.020 vs 0.204), use4 -> item 33 (0.101 vs 0.370). The four are separated chiefly by their appraisal-factor loadings (.429/.253/.200/-.161 observed vs .426/.248/.209/-.139 published), so no permutation of them survives. use5's largest loading is 0.411, below the paper's 0.45 retention cut-off, identifying it as one of the three dropped items -- consistent with 47 analysed items (eigenvalue sum 25.10 / 53.37% cumulative variance = 47.0). Live IRW per-item means equal the raw .sav column means to 1e-9 (use1 2.6976, use2 2.8127, use3 3.4192, use4 3.7251), tying the analysed columns to the shipped item codes. Factor 8 (numeracy) is excluded from the comparison because the .sav codes numeracy 1=correct/2=incorrect against the paper's correct-high orientation and that column does not reproduce. This does NOT establish any wording for use5 -- the article never prints it -- and it is not evidence about the instructions or the response anchors, which are whole-instrument text.
